texts.0221e3029219:
The first output will be the survey itself.  The applicant will send the PROMs questionnaire to prostate cancer patients in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland asking a variety of questions about their care and their quality of life. Those who respond will be sent a follow up questionnaires on an annual  a year later asking the same questions. The target date for the first mailing is 5th October 2015, with the fieldwork continuing for three years.  

Picker Institute Europe will present the research team at University of Leeds with a final data file once the fieldwork is complete from which the research team will carry out various analyses. This data file will consist of case data and will contain sampling information –, NHS trust and reference number - alongside the response data from the questionnaire.  The mailing data will not be included in this submission, so names, addresses, year of birth and NHS numbers will not be present. 

This data will contribute to a report presented to the funders:  Prostate Cancer UK and the Movember foundation and a series of papers submitted to peer-reviewed journals.  It is not yet known exactly what the articles will be on and where they will appear, but there is a large research team and it is hoped that there will be many outputs from this rich data source. 

** update December 2016 **

 The English Cohort part (Year 1) of the survey closed on 21st April 2016, with over 60% response rate. The Research Team in University of Leeds have received the final data file, so analysis is under way.
The next part of the Prostate Cancer project has already started. Mailings have been sent out for all Devolved Nations (Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales). There is currently no finalised closing date for any of these cohorts. The aim is exactly the same as for the English Cohort, so separate final data files per cohort will be collated and sent to the research team, in the same format as before.

texts.3e2a18c09803:
Picker Institute Europe requires a list cleaning service to conduct death checks and retrieve the following details: Patient forename, patient surname, patient address, and patient postcode.  In order to retrieve this information, the study team will be sending HSCIC a cohort file with the patient’s names, NHS number, and date of birth. Future applications requesting the same service for the same purpose/project will be made with larger samples. 
This service is required to prepare a mailing file for survey administration. The survey in question is a Patient Related Outcome Measures Survey (PROMS) of men diagnosed with prostate cancer. Picker Institute Europe has won the contract to carry this survey out from the University of Leeds, in collaboration with Oxford Brookes University, Queen’s University Belfast, University of Southampton and Public Health England.  They serve as the research team, themselves having won the funding from Prostate Cancer UK and the Movember Foundation, with Picker Institute Europe administering the project. 
It is a 3 year project during with an expected sample of a total 100,000 cancer patients but this is subject to change. The initial cohort is around 11,000 patients. The main aim of this project is to survey as many men as possible in all four UK countries who have had a diagnosis within the last 12-36 months. The survey will offer an insight into the quality of life of men who have been diagnosed and treated for prostate cancer.

texts.57caaac1c308:
Objective for processing:  To conduct death checks, retrieve patient addresses and data verification (of the data included in the CVS sent to HSCIC) for the purposes of administering a PROM survey of men with prostate cancer.

Processing activities: A csv file will be prepared to be sent to HSCIC for list cleaning with details of patient surnames and forenames, NHS numbers and date of births. Picker Institute Europe require HSCIC to identify those patients that have died as well as providing back the patient's NHS Numbers, forenames and surnames, addresses and postcodes.

Specific outputs expected, including target date: 
The first output will be the survey itself.  We will send the PROMs questionnaire to prostate cancer patients in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland asking a variety of questions about their care and their quality of life.  Those who respond will be sent a follow up questionnaire a year later asking the same questions.  The target date for the first mailing is 5th October 2015 , with the fieldwork continuing for three years.  Picker Institute Europe will present the research team at University of Leeds with a data file once the fieldwork is complete from which the research team will carry out various analyses. This will contribute to a report presented to the funders:  Prostate Cancer UK and the Movember foundation and a series of papers submitted to peer-reviewed journals.  It is not yet known exactly what the articles will be on and where they will appear, but there is a large research team and it is hoped that there will be many outputs from this rich data source. 

Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: 
Clinical and scientific progress in managing prostate cancer will only bring benefits in terms of well-being and survival for patients if we develop comprehensive and clinically meaningful approaches to measuring the important patient outcomes. 
Primary aims 
• To describe the Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQL, e.g., physical, psychosocial) of men with prostate cancer using qualitative and quantitative methods; 
• To explore if and how their HRQL is associated (cross-sectional) or is predicted by (longitudinal) disease, treatment and/or patient characteristics with a view to  inform development of health care policy and service delivery in ways that better meet the needs of such men and their families;
• To describe the levels of patient empowerment and undertake preliminary exploration of the interaction between patient empowerment and HRQL.
Secondary aims 
• To collect data to support, if possible, provider variation and health economic analyses especially for the longitudinal work;  
• To analyse the questionnaire data collected by exploring and checking the psychometric properties (e.g., reliability, validity) of the newer, less well-established questionnaire measures and to investigate the possibility of developing an item-bank for HRQL assessment for use with men living with and beyond prostate cancer using Rasch models. Qualitative interviews will be used to identify ‘gaps’ in surveys of importance to patients and patient partners with a view to adding additional items/questionnaires in the second surveys.
• To explore the acceptability/options of electronic PROMs data collection in this cohort and acceptability of real time feedback to service providers to influence/support direct patient care.  
The commercial aspect of this application does not, however, detract from the numerous and varied health-related benefits of the project, notably with regards to the insight into life with prostate cancer and intention to improve clinical treatment and policy going forward (see above). This work will ultimately inform clinicians and the NHS about prostate cancer sufferers and in turn help drive improvements to treatment. Picker Institute Europe is a health research charity, and this project supports the organisation's overarching objective to improve patient experience and healthcare.
texts.81def33ec1a7:
The University of Leeds requires a cohort of men with prostrate cancer to be list-cleaned  to provide up to date contact details as well as PDS data, which includes fact of death, to be supplied to the Picker Institute Europe for the purpose of administrating a PROM survey for use in the Life After Prostate Cancer Study.

A UK wide consortium of researchers, clinical experts and patients under the Movember Foundation Health Outcomes Improvement Initiative has developed the study.

The study is funded by Prostrate Cancer UK and Movember Foundation. The University of Leeds undertakes the role of the sponsor for this study.

Public Health England (PHE) and Welsh Cancer Intelligence and Surveillance Unit (WCISU) will supply cancer demographic data to Picker Institute Europe. Picker Institute Europe is an international charity working across social and health care.  No data for this project will flow outside of England and Wales.

Picker Institute Europe will supply patient identifiable data to NHS Digital. NHS Digital will disseminate identifiable data to Picker Institute Europe.

This is the first ever in-depth UK wide study of men diagnosed with prostate cancer. Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most common cancer (excluding melanoma) diagnosed in men in the United Kingdom (UK) and the number of men living with disease is increasing. Prostate cancer treatment can impact physically, psychologically and socially, affecting the health-related quality of life (HRQoL) of men and their partners/spouses. Therefore in addition to improving treatments it is important to measure outcomes reported to be of importance to patients, partners/spouses so that services can be tailored to meet men’s needs.

Using a series of linked projects the main aims of the LAPCD project are:

· To describe the HRQoL (e.g., physical, psychosocial) of men with prostate cancer using qualitative and quantitative methods;

· To explore if and how their HRQoL is associated (cross-sectional) or is predicted by (longitudinal) disease, treatment and/or patient characteristics with a view to inform development of health care policy and service delivery in ways that better meet the needs of such men and their families;

· To describe the levels of patient empowerment and undertake preliminary exploration of the interaction between patient empowerment and HRQoL.

Before the prostate cancer PROM surveys can be administered, patient addresses must be verified and death checks conducted. This is to ensure that the surveys are mailed to the correct address and that surveys are not mailed out to any deceased men. Death checks are conducted 48 hours prior to the date of the survey mail out. 

To date:

The first survey round (cohort 1) has been completed for England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. A cohort of men in Northern Ireland without prostate cancer were also surveyed. This “normative” data collected in Northern Ireland will provide baseline data to which the responses from the men with prostate cancer can be compared.
The study protocol indicated that those men who responded to the first survey would be resurveyed one year later to allow longitudinal assessment of outcomes. This resurvey has been completed in England, is currently underway in Northern Ireland and will begin next week in Scotland. The Welsh resurvey will be administered once all appropriate approvals are in place. 

In England a second cohort of men diagnosed one year after the first cohort (cohort 2) will also be surveyed to assess any changes to health service provision over time. Again, the cohort 2 surveys will be mailed out once the approvals are in place.

Update September 2017

Over three years this project has and will survey around 100,000 men about their experiences. In total, ten sets of surveys will be sent. This agreement (September 2017) relates to the ninth and tenth surveys; Wales Resurvey (Year 2) and Cohort 2. For each survey set Picker Europe will require 8 list cleans from NHS digital (16 in total).

Update December 2016

As data has only recently been received by the University of Leeds the benefits currently remain as above. With the follow up cohort, as NHS Digital will clean the data for patient objections which reduces the risk of sending the survey to men who have opted out under that model. The repeated fact of death check also reduces the risk of distressing the men's family by not contacting them if they are deceased.

Update August 2017 

The benefits remain as listed above. The England Cohort 2 arm will also provide the additional benefit of being able to test the suitability of using online methodology for this type of project. Response rate and non-response paradata will be considered to determine the appropriateness of contacting this demographic group using this methodology. 

Update September 2017  

This extension application (September 2017) relates to the ninth and tenth surveys; Wales Resurvey (Year 2) and English Cohort 2. 

During Cohort 1, the Research Team learnt a lot about the experiences of men post prostate cancer diagnosis, gaining an insight into short-term Health-Related Quality of Life, patient empowerment, and the interactions between these two facets of health care, as well as the appropriateness of paper PROMs data collection. The currently ongoing resurveys (yet to be completed in the devolved nations), are designed to assess the longer term impacts of a prostate cancer diagnosis. The English Cohort 2 (a predominately online methodology) will support in the initial primary aim of exploring the appropriateness and acceptability of electronic PROMs.
texts.aa296024c86d:
Although this is a UK wide study, the Northern Ireland Cancer Registry and the Scottish Information Service Division are responsible for conducting their own address checks and death checks using appropriate local services. The appropriate checks for England and Wales will be processed by NHS digital. 

Public Health England (PHE) and Welsh Cancer Intelligence and Surveillance Unit (WCISU) will send cancer demographic data to Picker Institute Europe. A csv file containing the patients full name, NHS numbers and date of births will then be prepared by Picker Institute Europe and sent to NHS Digital for list cleaning. Picker Institute Europe require NHS Digital to identify those patients that have died (non-identifiable fact of death only) as well as providing back the identifiable patient's NHS Numbers, forenames and surnames, addresses and postcodes.

Picker Institute Europe will utilise this data for the purposes of distributing survey packs. This data will be stored securely on password protected databases. All individuals, working under appropriate supervision on behalf of Picker Institute Europe, are subject to the same policies, procedures and sanctions as substantive employees. 

On completion of fieldwork, Picker Europe will submit a final data file, containing case data, sampling information (Trust details and reference number) alongside response data from the questionnaire. No mailing data (names and address) nor personal details (NHS numbers and year of birth) will be included in this file.  

In order to fully analyse and interpret the result, information provided by the respondent will be linked to other information in existing NHS databases, accessed by the National Cancer Registration and Analysis Service. The research team will receive anonymised disease and treatment information linked to survey responses. Personal information and survey responses will be stored as part of the cancer record by the National Cancer Registration and Analysis Service under the data handling rules for patient identifiable information.

The data will not be made available to any third parties other than those specified except in the form of aggregated outputs with small numbers suppressed in line with the HES Analysis Guide.

Update December 2016 

The identifiers for those men who consented to the original survey were flagged by the Picker Institute and Public Health England (PHE) informed to update their cohort details. This means that the data shared with NHS Digital will be for those men who consented only.  

PHE will send the cohort details (30,465) to the Picker Institute, who will then pass these onto NHS Digital for list cleaning with the same output as previously provided. Patient objections will apply.

Following the process of the first run, the cohort (split into part A (3000) and part B (27,645)) will be list cleaned multiple times. The first clean will occur once the agreement is approved to allow preparation of the survey once the cleaned data is received. Then subsequent cleans will be performed as needed (3x per cohort) as follow up letters are sent to the men regarding their response.

Update September 2017

This renewal (September 2017) relates to the ninth and tenth surveys; Wales Resurvey (Year 2) and Cohort 2. 

Wales Resurvey (Year 2)
The identifiers for those men who consented during the original (Year 1) survey were flagged by the Picker Institute and Welsh Cancer Intelligence and Surveillance Unit (WCISU) informed to update their cohort details. This means that the data shared with NHS Digital will be for those men who consented only.

WICSU will send the cohort details (2,522) to the Picker Institute, who will then pass these onto NHS Digital for list cleaning with the same output as previously provided: deceased checks; patient objections; NHS numbers; forenames and surnames; address and postcode information. 

Further deceased checks will be required prior to each of the six mailings (pilot invitation, pilot reminder, pilot final reminder, main mailing invitation main mailing reminder and main mailing final reminder). 

Cohort 2: De Novo
As identified in the protocol, this cohort of men diagnosed at a later date would be sent letter of invitation. PHE will send the cohort details (12,000) divided into two batches, a pilot (1,200) and a main (10,800), to the Picker Institute, who will then pass each of these onto NHS Digital for initial list cleanings with the same outputs as previously provided. Patient objections will apply. 

Further deceased checks will be required prior to each of the six mailings (3 mailings per batch – pilot and main).

All organisations party to this agreement are required to comply with the Data Sharing Framework Contract requirements, including those regarding the use (and purposes of that use) by “Personnel” (as defined within the Data Sharing Framework Contract ie: employees, agents and contractors of the Data Recipient who may have access to that data).

The first output will be the survey itself. The applicant will send the PROMs questionnaire to prostate cancer patients in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland asking a variety of validated questions about their care and their quality of life. Those who respond will be sent a follow up questionnaires one year later asking the same questions. The target date for the first mailing is 5th October 2015, with the fieldwork continuing for three years.  

Picker Institute Europe will present the research team at University of Leeds with a final data file once the fieldwork is complete. The research team will then carry out various data analyses. This data file will consist of case data and will contain sampling information, NHS trust and reference number - alongside the response data from the questionnaire.  The mailing data will not be included in this submission, so names, addresses, year of birth and NHS numbers will not be present. 

This data will contribute to a report presented to the funders:  Prostate Cancer UK and the Movember foundation and a series of papers submitted to peer-reviewed journals.  It is not yet known exactly what the articles will be on and where they will appear, but there is a large research team and it is hoped that there will be many outputs from this rich data source. 

All outputs will contain only data that is aggregated with small numbers suppressed in line with the HES Analysis Guide.

Update December 2016

The English Cohort 1 (Year 1) of the survey closed on 21st April 2016, with over 60% response rate. The Research Team in University of Leeds have received the final data file, so analysis is under way.
Cohort 1 mail-outs for the devolved nations (Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland) has already started. There is currently no finalised closing date for any of these cohorts. The aim is to replicate the process as for the English Cohort, so separate final data files per cohort will be collated and sent to the research team, in the same format as before.

Update July 2017

The England cohort 1 survey and resurvey is now complete, with a response rate of over 85% in the repeat survey. Final data was delivered to the Research Team on 14th July 2017.
The Devolved Nations cohort 1 survey has also been completed with final data delivered to the Research Team earlier this year. The Northern Irish resurvey is currently in field with the Scottish and Welsh resurveys expected to be rolled out the first week of September. In line with the study protocol, the final stage of the project is to invite a new cohort of men in England (cohort 2) diagnosed with prostate cancer at a later date to take part in an online survey.
Up to 12,000 men will be surveyed using primarily an online methodology. For those that wish, there will also be the ability to complete by paper. 
To cover the last part of this project (including the Wales Resurvey and the English Cohort 2, up to 16 deceased checks are required. 

Update September 2017

Surveys Summary Titles & Final data delivery/target dates

1) England (Year 1) - 27/05/2016
2) Northern Ireland (Year 1) - 24/01/2017
3) Scotland (Year 1) - 24/01/2017
4) Wales (Year 1) - 24/01/2017
5) Normative - 13/02/2017
6) England Resurvey (Year 2) - 14/07/2017
7) Northern Ireland Resurvey (Year 2) - in progress December 2017
8) Scotland Resurvey (Year 2) - in progress March 2018
9) Wales Resurvey (Year 2) - expected April 2018
10) Cohort 2: De Novo - expected April 2018

· Surveys 1-6 have been completed.
· 7 and 8 (Northern Ireland Resurvey (Year 2) and Scotland Resurvey (Year 2)) are in field.

This extension application (September 2017) relates to the ninth and tenth surveys; Wales Resurvey (Year 2) and England Cohort 2. 

The survey programme is not yet complete. However, the following conference papers have already been produced: 

March 2016: British Psycho Oncology Society Conference 
Change Processed in Men Navigating the PCa journey (Rivas et al.)
PCa and the Impact on Couples (Collaço et al.)
The Quality of Treatment Decision Making (Wagland et al.)
Presentation – Decision Regret (Wright et al.)

October 2015: Oxford Brookes Conference on Research Impact:
LAPCD Impact Conference Poster 2015 (Watson)

June 2015: National Intelligence Network Conference, Dublin
Effective Patient & Public Involvement in a Research Project (Butcher)
LAPCD¬ - Study Paper (Downing)

A webinar aimed at health professionals has been presented. The talk outlined the aims and methodology of the patient reported outcome measure. The webinar was hosted by Prostate Cancer UK.

This is proving to be a rich and varied data set, completion of the Wales resurvey and Cohort 2 surveys are only set to further advance this. 

The results of this research will be disseminated to both men and the clinicians treating them. The results of the research study will be published in academic journals and shared with NHS teams, commissioners and policy makers. As the work continues to progress, updates as to the survey and summary results are posted on the Life After Prostate Cancer Diagnosis website.

The final report of results will be submitted to Prostate Cancer UK and the Movember foundation in December 2018.  This will cover all findings of the study including: factors influencing planning and implementation and key findings. Once finalised, this will be published on the funders’ websites in early 2019.

It is expected that further academic paper(s) will be published in 2019. Target journals include: European Journal of Urology; New England Journal of Medicine; and the BMJ. All reports and findings will be publicised on the study and funders websites, providing links to open access papers, posters, presentations and webinars.
It is hoped that the findings will be presented at meetings and conferences to ensure the widespread dissemination of findings.
